sections.title: From personal mentor to corporate leadership: authenticity as a strategic priority

summary: This short talk uses a vivid hometown anecdote about a small-town shoe merchant to illustrate how deeply a business can be woven into a family's life. By gently guiding customers toward the right first shoes, accommodating tight budgets with a 'bring back the rest when you're in town' gesture, and treating the fitting moment as a meaningful service, the merchant becomes part of generations of family stories. The speaker then ties this lived example to leadership, crediting his father—the Des Plaines, Illinois shoeman—as the first to teach him the importance of being real. He argues that authentic, customer-centered care—embodied in everyday interactions—must scale in large organizations, and that the best leaders make this their most important job. The core message is that business growth should be anchored in staying present in customers’ lives, not just flashy marketing or transactional sales.
title: Be Part of the Story of Your Customer's Life: A Lesson in Customer-Centric Leadership
